summary.headline: Route Mobile FY26 gross margin rose to 22.9% as low-margin ILD exited, while revenue fell 3.7% to INR 44,082 mn; FY27 guided to mid-to-high single-digit growth.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations fell 3.8% YoY to INR 11,309 mn but rose 2.2% QoQ, with gross margin up to 23.3% from 19.3% as lower-margin ILD volume exited. Full-year FY26 gross profit crossed INR 1,000 crore for the first time (INR 10,073 mn, +5.9%), and adjusted EBITDA was flat at INR 5,259 mn (+0.4%) with margin at 11.9%. Management framed the call as a strategy update, citing ILD decline, AIT clean-up, enterprise budget cuts and integration complexity as headwinds, and set a five-pillar plan under Proximus Global. First-time FY27 guidance was given: mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth and EBITDA margin around 12%, alongside a dividend increase from INR 11 to INR 16.5 per share.

financial_highlights.value: around INR 1,400 crore as at March 31, 2026

segments.name: New products (RCS, WhatsApp, email, OTT)
segments.commentary: New products revenue was about INR 3,500+ mn in FY26, growing 11% YoY after a 43% CAGR since FY22, and comprised about 8% of total revenue. WhatsApp pricing was revised during the year, which lowered realisations despite rising volumes in India.

segments.name: Firewall / Network API (MNO solutions)
segments.commentary: Firewall revenue hit a record in the last month per management, and a large Claro deal is live. Revenue from A2P SMS Firewall is reported under the SMS segment, not under new products, and its mix was not disclosed.

segments.name: ILD (international long-distance A2P SMS)
segments.commentary: Management estimates ILD at about one-quarter to one-third of revenue. It is in secular decline but management says it has stabilised with no further drop in the last quarter's run rates.

segments.name: Domestic India
segments.commentary: Management says domestic volumes grew in India and rest-of-world, and new large domestic customers were added. Domestic ARPA is much lower than ILD, so the revenue per transaction fell while gross margin improved.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to grow by mid-to-high single digits; management said it will strive to overachieve.
EBITDA margin guided at around 12% for FY27, with strong EBITDA-to-cash conversion continuing.
Regular dividend to rise from INR 11 to INR 16.5 per share (50% increase), paid quarterly.
Organic capex described as not significant and roughly flat YoY.
Management expects recovery to start after the base effect, as domestic replaces ILD at lower per-message realisations.
capex_capacity: Organic capex is not meaningful and roughly flat YoY, mainly internal development for platform growth and omnichannel products.
M&A: management is evaluating a couple of targets, mainly small AI-led, capability-focused acquisitions; no size disclosed.
Management said vendor prepayments absorbed a meaningful amount of cash at year-end.
Treasury policy under review; management plans to move funds into higher-yielding fixed deposits.
demand_pricing: Revenue per billable transaction fell from 29 paisa to 25 paisa (about 14% decline), per the analyst's figures; management said pricing, not volume, drove the decline.
Management expects no sharp upward move in unit realisations as domestic volume grows, since domestic rates are lower than ILD.
RCS pricing is below SMS in some markets because of no interconnect arrangements among telcos; management hears telcos are discussing price increases.
Management says about 60% of the market is still SMS, with a shift to RCS and WhatsApp underway.
Management is targeting higher-margin solution-led deals and is declining low-margin bulk messaging volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why is new-product revenue only about 8% of revenue when peers report 30-35%, and is it a transition or an offering gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the platform covers WhatsApp, RCS, Viber and email and is not capability-constrained. Revenue was held back by WhatsApp price revisions, and the team is working on AI layers to lift adoption.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ILD share of revenue and is India termination falling?
qa_highlights.answer: ILD is about one-quarter to one-third of revenue. Management said ILD has stabilised in the last quarter, with domestic wins offsetting part of the loss.

qa_highlights.question: Can you give a volume split between domestic and overseas, and the margin difference for AI/solution products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a volume split or product-wise margins, citing competition. Firewall margins were said to range from 30% to 60-70% depending on engagement.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance of mid-to-high single digits and 12% margin only modest?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is the most likely scenario, that base effects will weigh on growth in the near term, and that internal initiatives aim to beat it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic capex and M&A plan, and why is cash building up with a yield below 4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic capex is not significant. M&A targets are small AI capability add-ons. Management agreed to revisit treasury policy for idle cash.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope of the network API opportunity and what were the trade receivable write-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the network API opportunity is early-stage and not quantified yet. Receivable write-offs were under INR 5 crore across small customers, about 0.4% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How will surplus cash be used, and does Proximus need to approve capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Route Mobile board makes these decisions, with a Proximus representative on the board. Cash is mainly earmarked for acquisitions, and the dividend was raised.

risks_watch: Continued ILD decline and whether management's claim that it has bottomed out holds in Q1 FY27.
WhatsApp and RCS pricing pressure, including the telco interconnect and price floor question.
FY27 revenue growth of mid-to-high single digits against a base that management says will require a longer period for domestic volume to offset ILD revenue.
Cash of about INR 1,400 crore earning a low yield, and how it will be deployed given the M&A timeline.
Limited disclosure: no split of domestic vs overseas volumes, firewall/network API revenue or product margins.
Related-party revenue from Proximus group entities (BICS and Telesign) under arm's-length agreements.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the margin and cash story, but guarded and sometimes evasive on disclosure: management declined to give product-wise margins, volume splits and the exact new-product mix. Management was candid about headwinds and admitted some were within its control. It also said guidance is a conservative first-time figure.
key_quotes: FY26 was the first time that our annual gross profit crossed INR 1,000 crores. That translated to a 22.9% gross profit margin for the year.
The reset was a difficult one. I believe it has made us more focused, more defensible business, and one that is well positioned for the next phase.
Our regular dividend will meaningfully increase from INR 11 per share to a sustainable level of INR 16.5 per share, which represents a 50% increase.

growth.why: First-time FY27 guidance of mid-to-high single-digit revenue growth (~7% midpoint) and ~12% EBITDA margin, backed mainly by domestic volume gains and a stabilising ILD base, with no specific capacity, order or contract figures given, so backing is vague.
